cards.a: The well-known mandatory BGP attribute that records the sequence of autonomous systems a route has traversed. It serves loop prevention (a route whose AS_PATH already contains my AS is discarded) and path selection (step 4 of the best-path algorithm, where shorter is preferred). Operators manipulate it with as-path prepend to steer inbound traffic.

cards.q: What are the two forms of AS_PATH?
cards.a: AS_SEQUENCE, an ordered list of ASes traversed such as 65010 65020 65030, and AS_SET, an unordered set such as {65010, 65020} that comes from aggregation.

cards.q: How does each eBGP advertisement treat the AS_PATH?
cards.a: Every eBGP advertisement prepends the local AS to the list; iBGP does not modify AS_PATH because the route stays within the same AS.

If a router's own AS appears anywhere in an incoming route's AS_PATH, the route is rejected because it has already passed through this AS. This makes BGP loop-free at the AS level even without split horizon.

cards.q: How does AS_PATH affect best-path selection and why prepend?
cards.a: The shorter AS_PATH wins when everything before it (weight, local-pref, origin) ties, at step 4. You cannot shorten a path, so prepending exists to make other paths appear longer and steer inbound traffic away.

cards.q: How do you prepend an AS_PATH with a route-map?
cards.a: route-map PREPEND permit 10 with match ip address prefix-list HOST and set as-path prepend 65001 65001 65001, applied to neighbor 192.0.2.2 with route-map PREPEND out. Prepend your own AS multiple times to make the path appear longer, and only prepend your own AS number.

cards.q: What do the AS_PATH regex symbols mean?
cards.a: ^ starts the AS_PATH, $ ends it, . matches any single character, _ matches a separator (space or brace), * means zero or more, + means one or more. ^65001$ means exactly one AS, ^65001_ means starts with 65001, and _65001_ means contains 65001.

cards.q: How do you filter routes by AS_PATH?
cards.a: Create an as-path access-list with ip as-path access-list 10 permit ^65001_ 65002$ and apply it to a neighbor with filter-list 10 in (or out).

cards.q: Command to test AS_PATH regular expressions?
cards.a: show ip bgp regexp ^65001 lists paths matching the regex; show ip as-path-access-list shows configured regex ACLs, and show ip bgp <prefix> shows the full AS_PATH per path.

Type well-known mandatory; job is loop prevention plus the step-4 tie-break; eBGP prepends the own AS while iBGP leaves it unchanged; prepend your own AS multiple times; AS_SET appears from aggregation only; filter with filter-list / ip as-path; shorter path wins.

cards.q: What does the regex pattern ^$ match?
cards.a: An empty AS_PATH, which indicates a locally originated route.

cards.q: When does an AS_SET appear in an AS_PATH?
cards.a: Only from aggregation (aggregate-address with as-set); normal advertisement produces AS_SEQUENCE. Do not expect AS_SET in ordinary BGP updates.
